correctness.rationale: For all integer N≥2, first reduce the sorting Lipschitz quotient to the finite maximum of permutation operator norms on the real mean-zero quotient. Path Laplacian eigenvalues λ_k=4 sin²(kπ/(2N)) give the ceiling cot(π/(2N)); the extreme eigenspaces are simple, with explicitly normalized cosine and alternating-sine eigenvectors. For even N these coordinate multisets coincide, giving attainment by an actual pair inside one ordering chamber. For odd N the low vector has a single zero coordinate but the high vector none, making saturation impossible. Sorted-rank matching with coordinatewise error at most π/(2N) gives the odd lower bound via the positive-semidefinite top-mode deficit matrix. The one-point inequality follows from crossing every sorted-value gap. A standalone checker reproduced 6,344 finite comparisons; the theorem does not rely on extrapolating finite checks.

originality.rationale: The result answers a different quantifier pattern than one-input graph Pólya–Szegő: sharp sensitivity of differences under simultaneous sorting of two unrelated signals. Primary full text on monotone-target Lp loss and graph/lattice rearrangements does not supply this explicit path two-point parity classification. Comparisons to Euclidean GroupSort, eigenvalue condition-number facts, a prior finite-star two-point theorem, and published finite-graph literature found no stronger prior implication. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not a guarantee that an unindexed historical calculation does not exist.

value.rationale: Sorting is a canonical monotone-rearrangement primitive on a finite path. Its one-point graph energy always drops, so linear-in-dimension two-point instability is a substantive conditioning phenomenon. The parity-sensitive exact saturation of a universal spectral ceiling and the tight odd-length asymptotic quantify the geometric obstruction. This is a natural path invariant, not arbitrary chosen parameters or a routine reparametrization of finite-star sorting.
